LibraryDescriptor.Name: Process Modeling Library
LibraryDescriptor.Description: Process Modeling Library supports discrete-event, or process-centric modeling paradigm. Using the Process Modeling Library you can model the real-world systems in terms of agents (entities, customers, products, parts, etc.), processes (sequences of operations typically involving queues, delays, resource utilization), and resources. The processes are specified in the form of flowcharts - a graphical representation used in many areas: manufacturing, business processes, logistics, healthcare, etc.

Variable.Name: choiceIsVolatile
Variable.Description:
Indicates that the condition value is stochastic and/or depends on volatile factors beyond the data contained within the incoming agent itself (e.g., the condition depends on the states of surrounding flowchart blocks).
Implementation note: Due to the pull-protocol implementation, this block may evaluate the condition twice: 1. First, when the agent is ready to exit a preceding block. This is necessary for routing decisions - to determine the recipient block for the agent. 2. Second evaluation may occur if the recipient block is currently busy and cannot receive the agent. In such a case, the agent remains in the preceding block. Later, when the agent is actually transmitted, the condition is evaluated again to ensure model correctness.
The block includes a check to detect undesired changes in the condition value between the two evaluations. If a change is detected, an error is raised, indicating that the agent cannot follow the initially selected route. When this parameter is enabled, the check is not performed, avoiding the second condition evaluation. This can help prevent false-positive errors caused by the natural variability of the condition.

Variable.Description: The unit task cannot be interrupted by any high priority task.

Variable.Name: PP_WAIT_FOR_ORIGINAL_RESOURCE
Variable.Description:
The unit task will be interrupted by any task with higher priority and will go into individual queue of resource unit.

recalculateAgentPriorityOld
Function.Description: Recalculates task priority for the given agent currently waiting in the queue of this block. This action may trigger preemption of resource units. Note, that there is special behavior in case when the seize policy of a seize block is set to 'seize units one by one'. In that case, if the agent already seized one or several units, some of the resource sets (needed to start a task) may be discarded (namely, the sets that can no longer be completed due to the units currently seized). Priority recalculation will NOT reset the discarded resource sets, that is the agent will only be elligible to seize units that are needed to complete non-discarded resource sets. Note, that in case of limited capacity of the queue of a seize block the recalculation will NOT affect the agents that are awaiting entrance to the seize block.

Function.Name: recalculatePriorities

Note, that there is special behavior in case when the seize policy of a seize block is set to 'seize units one by one'. In that case, if the agent already seized one or several units, some of the resource sets (needed to start a task) may be discarded (namely, the sets that can no longer be completed due to the units currently seized). Priority recalculation will NOT reset the discarded resource sets, that is the agent will only be elligible to seize units that are needed to complete non-discarded resource sets. Note, that the priorities will be only recalculated for the agents that are currently waiting in the queue of the seize block. That means that in case of limited capacity of the queue of a seize block the recalculation will NOT affect the agents that are awaiting entrance to the seize block.

Variable.Name: suspendResumeEntities

Variable.Description: Defines how the agents are picked up from the Queue block. The block can remove either All available agents from the Queue, or agents for which the Boolean condition is true. ActiveObjectClass.Description: NetworkStoragePut puts agent into a cell of a given storage or rack system. The agent is moved from its current location in the network to the cell location, optionally with the help of moving resources. Optionally, a delay may be associated with putting an agent into a cell.

Variable.Description: The unit task cannot be interrupted by any high priority task.

Variable.Name: PP_TERMINATE_SERVING
Variable.Description:
The unit task will be interrupted by any task with higher priority and will be terminated (forgotten).
Agent will not be suspended. It will just lose ALL resource units obtained in this Seize. Custom action may be defined using "On Task Terminated" (where the default action is remove agent from its current flowchart block)

Variable.Name: PP_SEIZE_ANY_RESOURCE
Variable.Description:
The unit task will be interrupted by any task with higher priority and will try seizing any other compatible resource.
Agent will be suspended until there is a resource for the task execution.

Variable.Name: PP_WAIT_FOR_ORIGINAL_RESOURCE
Variable.Description:
The unit task will be interrupted by any task with higher priority and will go into individual queue of resource unit.
Agent will be suspended until there is a resource for the task execution.

Variable.Name: PP_CONTINUE_WITHOUT_RESOURCE
Variable.Description:
The unit task will be interrupted by any task with higher priority and will be terminated (forgotten).
Agent will not be suspended. It will just lose ONLY one resource unit (which is being preempted). Custom action may be defined using "On Task lost unit" (where the default action is remove agent from its current flowchart block)

Function.Description: Returns true if a new agent may be accepted by the queue. Note that enabled preemption doesn't mean "queue is always open", and it that case this method also ensures queue capacity. This is because preemption works only for 'urgent' agents emitted by blocks using PUSH protocol (or from PUSH-only ports of other blocks).

Function.Name: free
Function.Description: Tells the queue to release the given agent and forward it to the 'out' port. Since this method is called, the agent may leave the Queue block via 'out' port, but it 'holds' the queue capacity until it is actually pulled from this queue block. Moreover, if the Queue block has corresponding configuration, the given agent may be preempted or it may exit queue by timeout during waiting on 'out' port. "On at exit" code is called for the given agent. This method returns true if the agent has been succesfully released and false in case when there is no such agent in the queue or the given agent is already exiting queue due to timeout or preemption or this agent is already waiting on 'out' port.

Function.Name: freeAll
Function.Description: Tells the queue to release all the agents and forward it to the 'out' port. This method returns true if any agent has been succesfully released and false in case when there is no agents in the queue or all of them are already exiting queue due to timeout or preemption or are already waiting on 'out' port.

Variable.Name: choiceIsVolatile
Variable.Description:
Indicates that the choice is stochastic and/or depends on volatile factors beyond the data contained within the incoming agent itself (e.g., the condition depends on the states of surrounding flowchart blocks).
Implementation note: Due to the pull-protocol implementation, this block may evaluate the condition twice: 1. First, when the agent is ready to exit a preceding block. This is necessary for routing decisions - to determine the recipient block for the agent. 2. Second evaluation may occur if the recipient block is currently busy and cannot receive the agent. In such a case, the agent remains in the preceding block. Later, when the agent is actually transmitted, the condition is evaluated again to ensure model correctness.
The block includes a check to detect undesired changes in the condition value between the two evaluations. If a change is detected, an error is raised, indicating that the agent cannot follow the initially selected route. When this parameter is enabled, the check is not performed, avoiding the second condition evaluation. This can help prevent false-positive errors caused by the natural variability of the condition.
